brief.headline: Federico has lost 5.7 kg (6.4%) since Sep 5 and has become withdrawn and low in mood since a close friend died, with day center attendance falling.

items.statement: Weight fell at every reading: 88.7 kg (Sep 5), 86.7 (Oct 1), 84.7 (Oct 28), 83.0 (Nov 24). That is a 5.7 kg (12.6 lb, 6.4%) loss in about 11 weeks. On Nov 24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The four weights and the -5.7 kg, -12.6 lb and -6.4% change match the vitals record. The dietitian note supports the appetite, skipped breakfast, 50% of lunches and the plan. Sep 5 to Nov 24 is about 11 weeks.

items.statement: On Nov 11 the day center reported he missed 4 of the last 8 scheduled days. When present he is quiet and leaves activities early. On Nov 13 he told the social worker he feels "down" and does not want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. The social worker plans a depression screen and grief support.
items.verifier_note: The Nov 11 attendance note and the Nov 13 social work note support every detail, including the planned depression screen and grief support.

items.statement: He went to the partner hospital ED on Sep 17 with chest pain and was admitted for 2 days. The cardiac workup was negative and no new medications were started. At the Sep 21 PCP follow-up he was back to baseline per his daughter, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The discharge summary and the encounter record support the Sep 17 ED visit, the 2-day admission, the negative workup and no new medications. The Sep 21 PCP note supports baseline per his daughter and close monitoring for two weeks.

items.statement: No flu vaccine is recorded for this season (season start Aug 1, 2026). The most recent flu vaccine on record was Apr 2, 2026.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season is false, the season start is 2026-08-01, and the latest flu vaccine is 2026-04-02.

questions_for_team: Who will complete the depression screen and start grief support, and by when?
Is the weight loss plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) enough, or does the team want other evaluation of the weight loss and poor appetite?
Should the team review his medications in light of the appetite and weight changes?
How can the team encourage day center attendance and meals, for example through transport or home-based support, while his mood is low?
Should the flu vaccine be offered now, given none is recorded this season?

checks: Confirm review window 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and identify the last IDT review date; pull all encounters, notes, and events in the window.

Falls and near-falls: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred while on anticoagulation (warfarin) or with orthostatic symptoms; flag for team discussion given osteoporosis and warfarin.
ED visits and hospital admissions: dates, diagnoses (especially heart failure exacerbation, atrial fibrillation, bleeding, syncope), and discharge plan adherence.

Medication changes since last review: new starts (donepezil/memantine ER capsule started 2026-08-31 is new just before window; verify tolerance and titration), stops, dose changes, and reconciliation across the many cardiac agents (metoprolol, carvedilol, verapamil, digoxin, losartan, furosemide, warfarin, simvastatin, alendronic acid).

Cardiac medication duplication review for team awareness: metoprolol succinate and carvedilol both listed as beta-blockers, and verapamil listed alongside metoprolol/carvedilol and digoxin; confirm with prescriber whether all are intended as active.
Anticoagulation monitoring: warfarin INR results and any out-of-range values, bleeding events, and dietary or interacting-medication changes.

Heart failure and weight trend: daily or weekly weights, edema, dyspnea, orthopnea, furosemide use, and any weight gain thresholds reached; review potassium and renal labs given losartan and furosemide.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend: resting and orthostatic readings, bradycardia or hypotension signals given beta-blocker, verapamil, digoxin, and losartan combination.
Digoxin-related checks: serum digoxin level and renal function if recorded, and any nausea, visual change, or confusion reported.
Cognition and behavior in Alzheimer's disease: MoCA/MMSE or other scores if done, delirium screen, agitation, wandering, sleep, and appetite changes since donepezil/memantine start.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, medication management, and meal preparation; review any therapy referrals.
Pain management: chronic low back pain and chronic pain scores, analgesic use including any NSAID use alongside warfarin, and mobility impact.
Bone health: osteoporosis care on alendronic acid (confirm administration instructions followed and dental status), any fracture events, and calcium/vitamin D status if documented.
Dental and sinus: loss of teeth status, dental visits, chronic sinusitis symptoms and treatments in the window; relevance to oral intake and nutrition.
Weight and nutrition given obesity (BMI 30+): weight trajectory, intake, and any dietary counseling; note the team should weigh this against heart failure fluid management.
Mood, social engagement, and attendance: depression or anxiety screens, program attendance, and any missed visits or calls.
Caregiver situation: primary caregiver status, strain, respite needs, capacity to manage medications and appointments, and any changes in living arrangement.

Care-plan items due in or near the window: assessments, reassessments, care-plan updates, consent or advance directive reviews, and goals of care discussion given progressive dementia and heart failure; list overdue items.
Labs and monitoring due: renal function, electrolytes, INR, lipid panel on simvastatin, and any other scheduled labs; flag any that are overdue or abnormal.

Summarize changes for IDT as questions for clinicians to decide, without recommending treatment changes; highlight the new AF, heart failure, and dementia diagnoses since enrollment as priority discussion items.
